name: Orrin Vasse
bio: Mother of the Bride-Weavers of Isseva, who has bound forty brides of reed for the flood and walked every one of them out to the mere. She has buried two husbands in the water and outlived the third, who went to Tollmere, which she counts the same. She does not believe the flood is coming back. She weaves the brides anyway, because it is the kind of thing you do not stop doing to find out.
unique_habit: Ties a knot in whatever is in her hands while she talks, and unties it when she has finished saying the thing, so that a long conversation with her leaves a cord with nothing in it.

appearance.notes: fingers cracked and stained green-gold from the reed, a weaver's bone needle through her plait

schedule.notes: binding next spring's bride on the withy frame
watching the bride, at the dusk

name: Ferrit Oache
bio: The wisp-catcher of the North Channel, who goes out on the fen at the dark of the moon with an eel-skin net and comes home with lights that never want oil. Isseva's lantern-wrights buy his jars and do not ask; the Reed Council would like to ask and has not. He was a lantern-wright's apprentice until he dropped a lantern on a burial jetty and watched what came out of the water to look at it.
unique_habit: Talks to the jars by number, never by name, and gets cross if anybody else gives them names.

appearance.notes: eel-skin gauntlets to the elbow, a ring of jar-stoppers on his belt, a faint green on his fingertips that does not wash off

schedule.notes: selling jars to whoever has the silver

name: Hesk Vaurel
bio: The last of the Tide-Watchers of Oulea, who have notched the gauge on the Builders' needle at every spring tide for two hundred years. She believes the Tide account the way other people believe the weather: the world is a shore and the sea went out and the sea comes back. She has worked out from her own notches roughly when, and has told nobody, because she does not want to be the woman who said it.
unique_habit: Measures everything in finger-breadths, including time.

appearance.notes: boots on, always; a notching-knife and a slate on a cord round her neck; salt in the creases of her face

schedule.notes: reading the night's tide off the float

name: Corra Hask
bio: The sixth Hask to walk rope on the island west of the Lantern Causeway, and the first to walk it alone. Her brother Iven went down to the Outfall nine years ago to ship with a Salt Isles trader who had come in out of season, and was not on her when she sailed, and was not anywhere. His rope is still on the rack with his name walked into it.
unique_habit: Counts her paces under her breath wherever she walks, because a ropewalker's paces are her measure; she can tell you how far Isseva is from anywhere in Hask paces.

appearance.notes: a leather palm-guard on her right hand, rope-burn scars up both wrists, tar under her nails

schedule.notes: laying the strands at the wheel
walking the sledge down as the rope lays

name: Edda Moye
bio: Keeper of the Unwinding south of Nauvissa for fifty years: she trims the reed hedges, rakes the path, and stands at the gate to tell the walkers which way is in. She has never walked it. Her husband and both her sons are in the water off Gullhithe and she says she is saving it, and that she will know when.
unique_habit: Rakes the path behind every walker who goes in, so that the only footprints in it are going out.

appearance.notes: a reed rake taller than she is, knuckles swollen, a ribbon of every colour tied round one wrist

schedule.notes: at the gate, for the walkers

name: Pell Oduin
bio: The heron-reader of the North Fen, who has sat in his hide by the dead alders every dawn for thirty years and chalked the flight on his slate for the Reed Council. He reads for anybody who will sit with him and does not pretend it is anything more than knowing where the herons went. The herons go to look at anything new in the fen, he says, so a heron-reader always knows where the news is.
unique_habit: Stands on one leg when he is thinking, and does not notice he is doing it.

appearance.notes: a coat sewn over with shed heron plumes, chalk on his fingers, very long legs

name: Nelle Saye
bio: The herb-wife of the east Delta, who grows sundews and pitcher-plants in peat beds under fly-nets and sells the dew to Isseva's lantern-wrights for glue and to its bleeders for salve. The Mother Sundew in the sunken tub by her door was her grandmother's and is the reason nobody steals from the garden.
unique_habit: Feeds the plants with tweezers and talks to the flies before she does it, apologising.

appearance.notes: a leather apron spotted with dew that never quite dries, a pair of bone tweezers on a cord, sticky fingers

schedule.notes: the Mother's eel, on a Fifthday

name: Wenna Corley
bio: Cook and tally-woman to the Great Dredge's crew, a Tollmere woman who came up the channel with the barge and stayed above at the change of shift to keep the board and the pot. The crew went down three weeks ago and did not come up. She has kept the pot on for them every night since, and the board, and has written to the Guild twice and been told to wait.
unique_habit: Moves the crew's pegs on the tally-board every morning and puts them back, because the Guild says the board is to be kept.

appearance.notes: the Guild's oxblood coat gone brown with the damp, a ladle and a tally-stick through her belt

schedule.notes: moving the pegs and putting them back
